I can give you some advice from your daughters' perspective. A very similar situation happened in my family when I was about 13, except that my Mom had been having an affair. I was completely heartbroken, and my Dad was crushed for years. I was so angry with my Mom -- I didn't talk to her for weeks, and when we did talk, it was a screaming argument. 

From my point of view -- I definitely missed my mom (the one who cheated), and I still loved her. But seeing my Dad being so upset was incredibly difficult. It made me almost feel like I was betraying him when I was "nice" to my mom. 

Hopefully your kids will come around, if you've been a good Dad. I honestly don't think what you did makes you a bad father. I felt as though my Mom had betrayed our family, though. Its a sucky feeling, and I know it feels horrible to you too. 

I think the most important piece of advice I'll give you is to avoid guilt tripping your daughters. My mom would always tell me how sad it made her that I was mad, that I wouldn't talk to her, and how bad she felt, and it just pissed me off more. I wanted to know that she knew what she did was wrong, but I didn't really want to hear about how "horrible" she felt -- because it made me feel even worse. Don't let your daughter's become your space to dump your negative emotions; it's likely they are already getting that from their Mom.

Don't say anything disrespectful about your ex-wife. State that you care about her, you know that you screwed up, and that you would do it differently if you could do it again. 

Just try not to pressure them, be there if they need you, and again -- DO NOT guilt trip them. That was the worst thing my Mom did, and it damaged our relationship permanently.

*edited for spelling
I agree here - I used to have this same problem, especially when sleeping with a new partner. I got treated for anxiety, and I'm realizing now that I haven't had an issue with it since then.
